digest.component_or_area: binding store recovery and retirement lifecycle
propositions: A crash after retired tombstone replacement but before live replacement leaves the same exact identity in both live and retired state, detectable but not safely completable at construction or preview time without violating read-only constraints.
The rich-text handler mutates entries obtained from all_bindings(), which must be cut to use the narrow facade operation instead.

Interrupted retirement recovery must be invoked at the validated write boundary in reconcile.py after the under-lock staleness gate and before the first remote issue fetch, reading only local binding state.

A durable tombstone is the authoritative retirement intent; explicit unretire removes it, while later automatic confirmations (200, clear_absent, same-key bind_confirm) do not implicitly resurrect a tombstoned identity.
Recovery completes only when tombstone, forward entry, and reverse entry identities agree exactly; any mismatch, corrupt live file, or replace failure aborts safely without unrelated mutation.

Construction, load, reconcile-check, dry-run, preview, selection, and filtered runs must perform zero writes for the retirement-completion operation, while existing create-recovery behavior remains pinned unchanged.
